volunteers-ae-uae-volunteering-platform.about:
Volunteers.ae, launched in 2017 as a partnership between the Emirates Foundation and the Ministry of Community Empowerment, is the main national platform connecting volunteers with opportunities across the UAE. Government entities, NGOs and companies post opportunities in Arabic and English, from events and community campaigns to environmental, educational and humanitarian work, both on site and virtual.

Students can build a verified record of volunteer hours and download certificates, which is useful for university applications, scholarships and school service requirements (such as IB CAS). Applications to each opportunity are reviewed within about five working days, and volunteering in Abu Dhabi may require a licence from the Department of Community Development, which the platform explains for each posting.

Registration is free and open to UAE citizens and residents of all nationalities and ages; volunteers under 18 need parent or guardian approval.
highlights: Official UAE platform with in-person and virtual opportunities
Logged volunteer hours and certificates for your CV
Open to all ages and nationalities living in the UAE
volunteers-ae-uae-volunteering-platform.eligibility: UAE citizens and residents of any nationality and age. Under-18s need parent or guardian approval. You need an Emirates ID and passport copy to register.
how_to_apply: Create an account on volunteers.ae (or sign in with UAE Pass) using Chrome on a computer.
Upload a photo, passport pages and Emirates ID (plus guardian approval if under 18).
Browse opportunities and apply to those that fit your interests.
Wait for the organiser's approval by email (up to 5 working days), then volunteer and collect your hours and certificate.

misk-startup-school-masterclasses.about:
Misk Startup School MasterClasses is a free-to-join online learning track on Misk Hub, the youth platform of Saudi Arabia's Misk Foundation. It consists of nine introductory masterclasses taught by founders and investors who have built and scaled startups: Strategic Thinking and Decision Making, Scaling and Growth, Entrepreneurial Mindset, Customer Acquisition, Business Models, Product Management, Market Validation, Funding, and Team.

Each masterclass takes roughly 1.5–2 hours and is self-paced, so you can fit it around school or university. Classes are in English with Arabic subtitles (and sign language). After completing the requirements and the post-assessment survey you can download a Misk certificate of attendance and share it on LinkedIn.

There are no prerequisites; it suits students curious about entrepreneurship, those preparing for startup competitions or incubators, and anyone wanting a structured introduction before joining an accelerator. Enrolment is open until 31 December 2026.
highlights: Nine masterclasses by real founders and investors
Self-paced, about 2 hours each; English with Arabic subtitles
Misk certificate of attendance
misk-startup-school-masterclasses.eligibility: Open to current and future entrepreneurs and anyone interested in entrepreneurship; no prerequisites. A Misk Hub account is required.
how_to_apply: Sign up on Misk Hub (hub.misk.org.sa) and create a profile.
Open the Startup School MasterClasses page and click "Enroll Now".
Complete the registration form before 31 December 2026.
Finish the masterclasses and the post-assessment survey to download your certificate.
misk-startup-school-masterclasses.costs: No fee is listed on the programme page.

one-million-prompters-dubai.about:
One Million Prompters is a Dubai initiative, backed by the Dubai Future Foundation and the Dubai Centre for Artificial Intelligence, that aims to train one million people in AI and prompt literacy over three years. Its core online course is hands-on and interactive and is split into four modules: Unleashing the Power of AI, Commanding Conversations with AI Chatbots, the AI-Powered Productivity Revolution, and Creative Frontiers with Generative AI (about three hours of video in total).

You learn how large language models and image generators work, how to write effective prompts, and how to use AI tools for study, productivity and creative projects, with a prompt-literacy certification as the learning outcome. The registration form accepts learners of any nationality and country of residence and asks for your school or university, so students are clearly part of the audience.

It is a quick, structured way to get practical AI skills and a credential from a Dubai government-backed initiative; it also links to Dubai's wider prompt-engineering community and events.
highlights: Four practical modules on AI, chatbots and generative AI
Self-paced online; about three hours in total
Open to learners worldwide; prompt-literacy certification
one-million-prompters-dubai.eligibility: Open to anyone; the registration form accepts all nationalities and countries of residence. English.
how_to_apply: Go to omp.dub.ai and click Register.
Create an account with your details (including school or university).
Work through the four modules at your own pace.
Complete the course to earn the prompt-literacy certification.
one-million-prompters-dubai.costs: No fee is shown on the course or registration pages.

elf-oup-story-writing-competition-2027.about:
The Oxford University Press Story Writing Competition is the Emirates Literature Foundation's flagship writing contest for young people. The 2026/27 theme is "Heroes": what does a hero look like to you? Stories can be written in English or Arabic, and must be original, unpublished and free of AI-generated content.

There are three age groups (age on 10 December 2026): 11 and under (up to 500 words), 12–14 (up to 1,000 words) and 15–18 (up to 1,500 words). Entries open on 9 June 2026 and close at 11:59 pm on 10 December 2026; winners are announced in February 2027 and receive their prizes in April 2027 at the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature in Dubai.

Each category winner receives a plaque, five copies of the published anthology and a free pass to festival sessions, and every entrant gets a certificate of participation. It is free, open to full-time school and homeschool students in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman, and is a good way to get published and recognised at the region's biggest literary festival (winners must attend the Dubai ceremony at their own expense).
highlights: Free; English or Arabic; theme "Heroes"
Winners published in an anthology and awarded at Emirates LitFest 2027
Open to students across the UAE and GCC
elf-oup-story-writing-competition-2027.eligibility: Full-time school or homeschool students aged up to 18 living in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait or Oman. One story per student. Winners must attend the Dubai prize-giving at their own expense.
how_to_apply: Write an original story on the theme "Heroes" within your age group's word limit.
Format it in a legible 12-point font with 1.5 line spacing, with a matching title.
Complete the online entry form on elfdubai.org and attach the story as a Word document.
Submit before 11:59 pm on 10 December 2026.

elf-readers-cup-2027.about:
Readers' Cup is the Emirates Literature Foundation's team reading competition. Schools enter teams of up to four students who read a shortlist of books and answer quiz questions about them. There are two age groups (recommended 11 and under, and 12–16) and separate Arabic and English competitions; each school can enter up to two teams per age group per language.

Registration runs 1 September – 10 November 2026. The first round is a virtual written quiz on 2 February 2027; the top 20 teams in each age group then compete in a live final during the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature in Dubai (14–20 April 2027).

There is no registration fee listed, but teams buy the first-round books from Magrudy's. It is open to full-time school and homeschool students in the UAE and the other GCC countries, and it is a fun, team-based way to build reading habits and compete at the region's largest literary festival.
highlights: Team quiz on a set reading list; Arabic and English competitions
Virtual first round, live final at Emirates LitFest
Open to schools across the UAE and GCC
elf-readers-cup-2027.eligibility: Full-time school or homeschool students in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait or Oman. Teams of up to four; up to two teams per school per age group per language. Winners attend the Dubai final at their own expense.
how_to_apply: Form a team of up to four students with a school coordinator.
Register online (English or Arabic form) before 10 November 2026.
Buy and read the first-round books (sold at Magrudy's).
Take the virtual first round on 2 February 2027; the top 20 teams per group go to the April final.
elf-readers-cup-2027.costs: No registration fee listed; teams buy the set books.

elf-poetry-for-all-2027.about:
Poetry For All, sponsored by Emirates NBD, is the Emirates Literature Foundation's recitation competition. Students learn a poem from the approved list for their age group by heart and perform it on stage without notes; students aged 14–18 also give a short (one-minute) justification of their choice. Categories are 8–13, 14–18 and Students of Determination (8–18), in Arabic or English.

Schools first hold an internal round and then register up to two students per age group per language by 12 November 2026. Semi-finals take place on 11–18 January 2027 in Dubai, 19–21 January in Abu Dhabi, and 25 January in Dubai for Students of Determination. The final round and prize-giving take place during the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature (14–20 April 2027).

It is free and builds public speaking, confidence and a love of poetry; every semi-finalist receives a certificate and winners receive plaques at the festival.
highlights: Memorised poetry performance in Arabic or English
Semi-finals in Dubai and Abu Dhabi; final at Emirates LitFest
Inclusive Students of Determination category
elf-poetry-for-all-2027.eligibility: UAE residents who are full-time school or homeschool students aged 8–18 on 12 November 2026. Up to two students per school per age group per language; Arabic or English, not both.
how_to_apply: Take part in your school's internal round.
Your school coordinator registers you and your chosen poem online by 12 November 2026.
Memorise a poem from the approved list for your age group.
Perform at the January 2027 semi-final; finalists perform at the festival in April.

elf-letter-writing-competition-2027.about:
The Emirates Literature Foundation's Letter Writing Competition celebrates handwriting and the art of a well-crafted message. For 2027 the theme is "Heroes": write to someone you want to thank, honour or better understand, whether a person you know, a historical figure or a fictional character.

There are three age categories (8–10, 11–13, 14–18). Letters of 200–400 words are handwritten on one side of a single A4 sheet in pen, scanned (not photographed) and uploaded as a PDF through the online form, in Arabic or English. AI-generated content is not allowed. The deadline is 11:59 pm on 8 January 2027.

First-place winners get a meet-and-greet with an Emirates LitFest 2027 author, plus book vouchers, a plaque and a festival pass; all entrants receive a certificate of participation. It is a quick, free entry that suits younger writers.
highlights: Free; theme "Heroes"; Arabic or English
Winners meet a festival author and win book vouchers
Three age categories from 8 to 18
elf-letter-writing-competition-2027.eligibility: Full-time school or homeschool students aged 8–18 living in the UAE. One letter per student.
how_to_apply: Handwrite a 200–400 word letter on one side of an A4 sheet in pen.
Scan it clearly as a PDF (photos are not accepted).
Complete the online entry form on elfdubai.org and upload the PDF.
Submit before 11:59 pm on 8 January 2027.

elf-book-in-a-box-2027.about:
Book in a Box is the Emirates Literature Foundation's class project for primary schools. Guided by their teacher, a class chooses an age-appropriate book and recreates the book, or one scene from it, as a diorama made mainly from recycled or natural materials.

Teachers submit 3–5 photos, a short blurb about the book and why it was chosen through the online form between 1 September 2026 and 25 February 2027. Shortlisted dioramas are displayed at the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature (14–20 April 2027), where final judging (creativity, imagination, originality, use of recycled materials and relevance to the book) and prize-giving take place.

Prizes are plaques and Magrudy's book vouchers (AED 1,000 for first place and the Visitors' Choice award, AED 750 and AED 500 for second and third), and every participant receives a certificate.
highlights: Whole-class creative project using recycled materials
Shortlisted work exhibited at Emirates LitFest 2027
Book-voucher prizes up to AED 1,000
elf-book-in-a-box-2027.eligibility: Primary school classes at schools in the UAE (full-time students, UAE residents). One entry per class; several classes per school may enter.
how_to_apply: Choose a book as a class and build the diorama.
The teacher completes the online registration form (opens 1 September 2026).
Upload 3–5 images, a short book blurb and why it was chosen by 25 February 2027.

elf-digital-storytelling-competition-202.about:
The Al-Futtaim Digital Storytelling Competition (Visual Word Award) challenges teams of up to four high-school students aged 14–18 to adapt part of an Arabic book or poem into a 2–3 minute film. Teams can use acting, animation, narration or any creative approach, but the dialogue or narration must be in their own voices in Modern Standard Arabic. Texts come from the competition lists or any published Arabic work linked to sustainability, environment, well-being or cultural diversity.

Films (1080p, 30 fps or more, shot on phones or cameras) are uploaded with a digital poster and a short summary through the online form by 11:59 pm on 2 March 2027. Shortlisted teams meet the judges at the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature in April 2027, where awards are presented.

First place wins the chance to work with a local production studio, a shield and an AED 1,000 book voucher; second and third receive shields and AED 500 vouchers. It is ideal for students interested in film, media and Arabic literature.
highlights: Make a 2–3 minute film from an Arabic book or poem
Winners work with a local production studio
Teams of up to four; phones are fine for filming
elf-digital-storytelling-competition-202.eligibility: Students aged 14–18 who live in the UAE and study full-time at UAE schools (or homeschool). Teams of up to four. Arabic-language competition.
how_to_apply: Form a team and choose an Arabic text from the lists (or a qualifying published work).
Shoot and edit a 2–3 minute film in Modern Standard Arabic with a digital poster.
Upload the film and summary through the online form by 2 March 2027.

hub71-access-programme-cohort-21.about:
Hub71 is Abu Dhabi's global technology ecosystem, backed by Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi government. Its Access Programme is a 12-month package for pre-seed to Series A startups that want to set up in Abu Dhabi and scale globally: a four-week launch phase, market-entry preparation, growth acceleration (including a three-month guided track powered by Techstars), a fundraising showcase and a public Demo Day.

Selected startups receive AED 250,000 in in-kind incentives (office space, health insurance, housing, licensing and visa support, legal, financial and marketing services) and AED 250,000 in cash in exchange for equity via a SAFE, with a top-up of up to AED 250,000 for high performers. At least one founder must relocate to Abu Dhabi long term and build a team there.

The current deadline is February 2027 for a cohort starting in September 2027; applications are reviewed by April and late applicants are considered for the next cohort. This is a serious option for student or recent-graduate founders with traction who are ready to move to the UAE.
highlights: AED 250k in-kind support plus AED 250k cash via SAFE
Housing, office, health insurance and visa support in Abu Dhabi
Techstars-powered guided track and Demo Day
hub71-access-programme-cohort-21.eligibility: Pre-seed to Series A tech startups from any country. At least one founder must relocate to Abu Dhabi long term. A PDF pitch deck is required.
how_to_apply: Prepare a PDF pitch deck (problem, solution, traction, team, plans for Abu Dhabi).
Complete the online application at hub71.com/program/access-programme/apply.
If shortlisted, pitch to the Hub71 team and partners in rounds 2 and 3.
Await the selection committee decision (reviews by April 2027).
hub71-access-programme-cohort-21.costs: No application fee. Cash investment is in exchange for equity (SAFE note).

hub71-initiate-programme.about:
Initiate is Hub71's programme for very early founders, at the ideation or pre-MVP stage, which makes it the most accessible Hub71 track for students and recent graduates with a strong idea. Founders apply to one of Hub71's venture-builder partners (such as SC Ventures, Fikra Ventures or TMC2) according to their sector, and the venture builder helps build the MVP and go-to-market strategy.

Hub71 provides a free licence and office space for the first year (the venture builder covers year two), soft-landing guidance in Abu Dhabi, proximity to ADGM's regulatory framework, access to 150+ partners and service providers, and Hub71+ community events. Once milestones are reached, startups can apply to the Hub71 Access Programme.

Priority sectors are FinTech and digital assets, ClimateTech, life sciences, EdTech, mobility and logistics, and FoodTech, with AI-enabled startups encouraged. Hub71 itself takes no equity and gives no direct funding; venture builders set their own funding and equity terms, so read them carefully.
highlights: For idea and pre-MVP founders
Free licence and office in Abu Dhabi for year one
Pathway to the Hub71 Access Programme
hub71-initiate-programme.eligibility: Early-stage founders at ideation or pre-seed stage building in Hub71 priority sectors (FinTech, ClimateTech, life sciences, EdTech, mobility, FoodTech; AI encouraged). Nationality is not restricted.
how_to_apply: Choose a venture-builder partner that fits your sector.
Apply via hub71.com/program/initiate/apply.
Pass Hub71's programme-fit check and the venture builder's interviews.
Onboard, relocate/soft-land in Abu Dhabi and start the venture-builder programme.
hub71-initiate-programme.costs: No fee; Hub71 takes no equity. Venture builders usually take equity on their own terms.

sharjah-entrepreneurship-festival-2027.about:
The Sharjah Entrepreneurship Festival (SEF) is the annual flagship event of Sheraa, the Sharjah government-backed entrepreneurship centre. The 2027 edition takes place on 30–31 January 2027 at SPARK in Sharjah and brings together founders, investors, tech innovators, creatives, aspiring entrepreneurs and students.

The programme typically includes keynote talks and panels, hands-on workshops, an investor lounge, a startup showcase, the Seffy Awards, a children's "Little Founders" area and the SEF Pitch Competition, in which startups pitch for prize funding (advertised at AED 200,000–275,000). It is a strong place for student founders to learn, network and find mentors in the UAE ecosystem.

Passes are sold online with student tickets, and prices increase closer to the event. Sheraa also runs student programmes such as the eight-week Startup Dojo for students and aspiring founders, so the festival is a good entry point into its ecosystem.
highlights: Two-day festival with talks, workshops and investor networking
SEF Pitch Competition with six-figure AED prize pool
Student passes; gateway to Sheraa's student programmes
sharjah-entrepreneurship-festival-2027.eligibility: Open to anyone with a pass; student tickets available. Pitch competition is for startups (check the SEF site for criteria and deadline).
how_to_apply: Buy a festival pass (student pass) on sharjahef.com, early for the lowest price.
If you have a startup, check the SEF Pitch Competition page for the application window.
Plan your sessions and workshops and attend on 30–31 January 2027 at SPARK, Sharjah.
sharjah-entrepreneurship-festival-2027.costs: Paid passes (student tickets available; price not published on the homepage). Travel and accommodation are your own.

cwmun-emirates-2027.about:
Change the World Model United Nations (CWMUN) is a large international MUN circuit run by the Italian non-profit Associazione Diplomatici and Change the World Academy, with conferences in New York, Rome, Paris, Singapore and elsewhere. CWMUN Emirates 2027 will take place in Abu Dhabi in April 2027 (exact dates and venue to be confirmed) for roughly 2,000 students, with the theme "Renewable Energy Diplomacy: a sustainable path to a global future".

There are three age levels: middle school (9–13), high school (14–18) and university (18–28). Participants represent countries in simulated UN committees, and selected students must complete a mandatory online preparatory course before attending. Hotels in Abu Dhabi and Dubai are being arranged by the organiser, and you can register as an individual or with a school/university group.

Admission is selective: you submit an application and do a short interview with Change the World Academy staff. Merit-based grants can reduce enrolment fees or cover conference participation. Airfare and visas are not included; the organiser can issue an invitation letter for the UAE visa.
highlights: Around 2,000 delegates from many countries; theme Renewable Energy Diplomacy
Middle-school, high-school and university levels
Merit-based grants available; individuals or groups
cwmun-emirates-2027.eligibility: Students aged 9–28 of any nationality (middle school, high school or university). Selection interview and completion of the mandatory preparatory course required. English.
how_to_apply: Submit an application on the CWMUN Emirates page (individual or group).
Complete the selection interview with Change the World Academy staff.
If selected, enrol, apply for a merit grant if needed, and complete the preparatory course.
Arrange your UAE visa (invitation letter available on request) and travel.
cwmun-emirates-2027.costs: Enrolment fee (not published on the page) with optional accommodation packages; airfare and visa not included. Merit-based grants can reduce or waive fees.

kaust-taqadam-startup-accelerator.about:
TAQADAM is KAUST's startup accelerator, run with SAB (Saudi Awwal Bank) since 2016. It starts with a pre-accelerator bootcamp; teams selected after the bootcamp receive USD 40,000 and enter a six-month programme of mentorship, workshops and in-person activities at KAUST. At the annual showcase, ten startups secure follow-on funding of USD 100,000, and the most promising can qualify for further pre-seed investment.

Teams also get co-working space, subsidised design, finance and legal services, and help incorporating in Saudi Arabia (for international founders). It is open to all nationalities and industries, with no age limit, and accepts both early- and late-stage startups, which makes it accessible to student and graduate founders.

You need at least two founders and evidence of progress (customer interviews or signed interest), at least one founder able to attend all required activities, and university permission if you use university IP. International teams need a realistic plan to expand to Saudi Arabia within a year. Cohort dates are announced on the TAQADAM site; register your interest to be notified.
highlights: USD 40,000 for teams selected after the bootcamp
USD 100,000 follow-on funding for ten startups at the showcase
Open to all nationalities and ages; co-working at KAUST
kaust-taqadam-startup-accelerator.eligibility: Teams of at least two founders, any nationality, industry or age, with evidence of progress. Not enrolled in another accelerator at bootcamp start. International startups must plan to expand to Saudi Arabia within one year.
how_to_apply: Register your interest on taqadam.kaust.edu.sa (HubSpot form) or email Apply.Taqadam@kaust.edu.sa.
Apply when the next cohort opens, showing traction and your team.
Attend the pre-accelerator bootcamp if selected.
Teams selected after the bootcamp receive funding and join the six-month programme.
kaust-taqadam-startup-accelerator.costs: No fee listed. Funding terms (USD 40,000 and follow-on) are set by the programme; check equity terms when applying.

khalifa-university-young-future-energy-l.about:
Young Future Energy Leaders (YFEL) began in 2010 as part of Masdar Institute's outreach and is now run by Khalifa University in Abu Dhabi. It is a year-long programme for students and young professionals who want to lead in energy and sustainability: participants take a sequence of courses (Foundation, Advanced Exploration, Leadership and Application, the role of policy in renewable energy, entrepreneurship, and being a future leader), along with workshops, debates and panels.

The programme includes case competitions and project sprints, site visits and international engagements, mentorship and career exposure; members traditionally take part in Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week and the World Future Energy Summit. Graduates receive a certificate of completion and join the YFEL alumni community.

It is aimed at advanced undergraduates, master's students and early-career professionals with strong English, from the UAE and abroad. KU lists registration for the 2027 cohort opening on 11 January 2027; check the YFEL site or email yfel@ku.ac.ae for the exact requirements before applying.
highlights: Year-long energy, climate and policy leadership track
Case competitions, site visits and mentorship
Linked to Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week; certificate and alumni network
khalifa-university-young-future-energy-l.eligibility: Advanced undergraduate students, master's students and early-career professionals interested in energy and sustainability, from the UAE or abroad. Strong English required.
how_to_apply: Check the YFEL site for the 2027 call (registration listed as opening 11 January 2027).
Register through KU's portal (pgapply.ku.ac.ae/register/YFEL).
Complete any selection task (past cohorts were selected through a case-study competition).
Attend the programme activities in Abu Dhabi through the year.
khalifa-university-young-future-energy-l.costs: No fee is listed; participants are responsible for their own travel to Abu Dhabi activities unless KU states otherwise.

adek-rize-university-preparation-career-.about:
Rize UPCG is the Abu Dhabi Department of Education and Knowledge's university-preparation and career-guidance programme for UAE national students in grades 9–12 (years 10–13) across Abu Dhabi. It is designed to help students discover their interests, plan their futures and prepare strong university applications in the UAE and abroad.

The programme has four strands: Future Planning (exploring interests, identifying strengths and building skills); University Guidance (exploring degrees and universities, standardised-test preparation and application support); Counsellor Support (dedicated advisors, career exploration and scholarship applications); and Extracurricular Activities (industry projects, hands-on work experience, portfolio building and ADEK Summer Programs).

It is free and students can register online at any time through the ADEK page. For Emirati students in Abu Dhabi it is one of the most direct routes into ADEK's summer programmes and scholarship guidance.
highlights: Free university and career guidance with dedicated advisors
Test preparation and application and scholarship support
Access to industry projects and ADEK Summer Programs
adek-rize-university-preparation-career-.eligibility: UAE national high-school students in grades 9–12 (years 10–13) in Abu Dhabi.
how_to_apply: Open the Rize UPCG page on adek.gov.ae.
Click "Register to the Rize UPCG program today!" and complete the form.
Work with your assigned advisor on future planning, testing and applications.

duke-karsh-international-scholars-2027.about:
The Karsh International Scholars Program, funded by Bruce and Martha Karsh, is Duke University's top award for students who are not US citizens. Each year it selects high-achieving international first-years who also have financial need, and it currently has scholars from more than 20 countries, from Botswana and Egypt to Pakistan and Vietnam.

The scholarship covers tuition, room and board, mandatory fees and any demonstrated need beyond those costs, so a Karsh Scholar pays nothing for the four-year degree at one of the top private universities in the US. Scholars also receive funding for three summers of research, unpaid internships or similar experiences, and join an enrichment programme run by Duke's Office of University Scholars and Fellows.

There is no separate application and no nominations: you apply to Duke as a first-year (Early Decision by 2 Nov 2026 or Regular Decision by 4 Jan 2027) and request need-based aid in that same application. International students who do not request aid at the point of admission cannot get Duke funding later, so tick the box.
highlights: Full cost of attendance plus any extra demonstrated need
Funding for three summers of research or internships
No separate application: apply to Duke and request aid
duke-karsh-international-scholars-2027.eligibility: Citizens of any country other than the US (dual US citizens are not eligible) applying as first-year undergraduates who do not already hold a bachelor's degree. Applicants must demonstrate financial need and request aid in their first-year application. Strong academics are expected; English proficiency is required for non-native speakers.
how_to_apply: Apply to Duke via the Common App or QuestBridge by 4 Jan 2027 (Regular Decision) or 2 Nov 2026 (Early Decision)
Indicate in the application that you are applying for need-based financial aid
Submit the CSS Profile and Duke's financial aid documents (RD: by 1 Feb 2027)
Admitted applicants with need are reviewed for the Karsh Scholarship; no separate essay is required
duke-karsh-international-scholars-2027.costs: Tuition, room and board, mandatory fees and demonstrated need above those costs, for four years, plus three summers of funded experiences. Duke's application fee (about US$85) applies unless waived.

emory-university-scholar-programs-2027.about:
The Emory University Scholar Programs are Emory's merit scholarships for first-year students, led by the Robert W. Woodruff Scholarship, which at its top level covers full tuition, fees, housing and meals. Scholars study either at Emory College in Atlanta or at Oxford College (a two-year liberal arts campus that feeds into Emory College), and join a community with early registration, special programming and faculty mentorship.

About 10,000 students opt in each year and 175–200 become finalists. Awards range from partial to full scholarships and are renewable for eight semesters. Emory states clearly that first-year, home-schooled and international applicants can apply regardless of citizenship. Finalists are interviewed in spring (an on-campus visit for US-based finalists).

The key point is timing: you must submit your full Emory application by 15 November 2026 (1 November for Early Decision I) even if you apply Regular Decision, and answer 'Yes' to the Scholar Programs question. Students not chosen are still considered for admission and for other merit awards.
highlights: Awards from partial up to full tuition, fees, housing and meals
Open to international applicants regardless of citizenship
Just tick 'Yes' on the application: no separate form
emory-university-scholar-programs-2027.eligibility: First-year applicants of any citizenship, including international and home-schooled students. Selection is based on academic excellence, leadership and character as shown in the application. English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo) is recommended if English is not your first language.
how_to_apply: Create a Common App account and add Emory University
Answer 'Yes' to the question about the Emory University Scholar Programs
Submit the complete application by 15 Nov 2026 (ED II/RD) or 1 Nov 2026 (ED I)
If named a finalist (late February), take part in the spring finalist interviews
Apply separately for need-based aid if you also need it
emory-university-scholar-programs-2027.costs: From partial scholarships up to full tuition, fees, housing and meals for eight semesters (top Woodruff level). Merit is applied before any need-based aid.

vanderbilt-signature-merit-scholarships-.about:
Vanderbilt University in Nashville awards its signature merit scholarships to roughly the top 1% of first-year applicants. The Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship gives full tuition plus a one-time summer stipend for an immersive experience after the sophomore or junior year; the Ingram Scholars Program adds a focus on community service and social impact. Applying for the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship also puts you in the pool for additional merit awards (Carell Family, Curb Leadership, Fred Russell–Grantland Rice).

Vanderbilt's scholarship FAQ states that international applicants are eligible to receive any of its merit scholarships, and test scores are optional for fall 2027 scholarship consideration. Financial need is not a factor, but Vanderbilt meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted students who apply for aid, so need-based aid can top up the tuition award.

After you submit the Common App, Coalition or QuestBridge application, you receive a MyAppVU account where you upload the scholarship essays. Everything must be submitted by 1 December 2026, whichever admission round you choose. Awards renew yearly with at least a 3.0 GPA.
highlights: Full tuition for four years plus a summer stipend
International applicants eligible for all merit scholarships
Test-optional for fall 2027 scholarship review
vanderbilt-signature-merit-scholarships-.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality applying to Vanderbilt for fall 2027. Selection is based on academic achievement, intellectual promise, leadership and contribution outside the classroom. Blair School of Music applicants are also judged on auditions.
how_to_apply: Submit the Common App, Coalition or QuestBridge application to Vanderbilt
Activate your MyAppVU account (emailed 2–3 days after you apply)
Under the Scholarship tab, choose the Cornelius Vanderbilt and/or Ingram programme and upload your essays by 1 Dec 2026
Also apply for need-based aid (CSS Profile) if you need help beyond tuition
Recipients are notified at the end of March 2027
vanderbilt-signature-merit-scholarships-.costs: Full tuition for eight semesters plus a one-time summer stipend; housing, meals and travel are not covered by the merit award (need-based aid can cover them).

washington-and-lee-johnson-scholarship-2.about:
The Johnson Scholarship at Washington and Lee University (W&L), a highly ranked liberal arts university in Lexington, Virginia, is one of the most generous merit awards in the US. It covers tuition and fees, housing and food (worth over US$89,000 a year) plus US$10,000 in summer enhancement funds for internships, research or travel. Students with additional need can receive more.

Up to 44 incoming students (about 10% of the class) become Johnson Scholars each year. The Johnson application also serves as the application for all other W&L merit scholarships. W&L's international admissions page lists the Johnson deadline alongside the regular international requirements, and international applicants must send English proficiency documents by the same 1 December date.

Finalists are invited to an on-campus selection weekend (costs paid by W&L) where they stay with a current scholar, attend classes and interview. Winners are notified by mid-March 2027.
highlights: Tuition, fees, housing and food plus US$10,000 for summers
Up to 44 awards a year (~10% of the class)
Expenses-paid finalist weekend
washington-and-lee-johnson-scholarship-2.eligibility: First-year applicants to W&L, including international students. You must submit the Common Application and the Johnson Scholarship supplement (a second personal essay) by 1 Dec 2026; non-native English speakers must send English proficiency documents by the same date.
how_to_apply: Submit the Common App to Washington and Lee (ED I, ED II or RD)
Complete the Johnson Scholarship supplement with its extra essay by 1 Dec 2026
International applicants: send English proficiency results by 1 Dec 2026
Send any additional supporting materials by 15 Dec 2026
If selected as a finalist, attend the selection weekend; decisions by mid-March
washington-and-lee-johnson-scholarship-2.costs: Full tuition and fees, housing and food (over US$89,000 a year) plus US$10,000 summer enhancement funding, for four years.

tulane-global-scholarships-2027.about:
Tulane University in New Orleans reserves its Global Scholarships for international first-year students. These merit awards may cover full tuition and fees or even the full cost of attendance, and renew for four years (five for the architecture programme). Tulane also offers partial merit awards open to all applicants and up to US$30,000 of need-based aid for international students.

There is no separate essay: the international admission committee nominates candidates based on the Common Application and the CSS Profile. Applicants in roughly the top 20% academically are most competitive, and submitting test scores is preferred though not required. Some candidates are invited to a video interview by 31 March.

To be competitive you must apply early: Early Action by 10 November 2026 or Early Decision by 1 November 2026, plus the CSS Profile and Tulane's Declaration & Certification of Finances.
highlights: Can cover full tuition and fees or full cost of attendance
Reserved for international first-years
No separate scholarship essay: nomination from your application
tulane-global-scholarships-2027.eligibility: Non-US citizens applying as first-year students. Strong academic record (top 20% of applicants most competitive); test scores preferred but optional. Must apply Early Action or Early Decision and submit the CSS Profile.
how_to_apply: Submit the Common App to Tulane by 10 Nov 2026 (Early Action) or 1 Nov (ED)
Complete the CSS Profile
Submit Tulane's Declaration & Certification of Finances
Respond if invited to a video interview (by 31 March)
tulane-global-scholarships-2027.costs: Up to full tuition and fees, and in some cases full cost of attendance, renewable for four years.

boston-university-presidential-scholarsh.about:
Boston University, a large private research university in the heart of Boston, awards the Presidential Scholarship to first-year students from around the globe who show exceptional academic achievement as well as talent, initiative, creativity and impact in their school or community. From students entering in fall 2026, the award is worth half tuition each year and renews for four years.

BU's merit page lists the Presidential Scholarship under both 'US citizens and permanent residents' and 'International students'. There is no separate application: the only requirement is to complete your BU admission application by 1 December 2026. International students should note that BU's need-based aid for non-US citizens is very limited, so plan to cover the remaining half of tuition plus living costs.
highlights: Half tuition every year for four years
Open to international students
Only requirement: apply to BU by 1 December
boston-university-presidential-scholarsh.eligibility: First-year applicants from any country with exceptional academic records, considered automatically if the BU application is complete by 1 Dec 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply to Boston University through the Common App
Make sure your application is complete by 1 Dec 2026
No extra scholarship form is needed; recipients are told with their admission decision
boston-university-presidential-scholarsh.costs: Half tuition per year (renewable); housing, meals and other costs are not covered.

richmond-scholars-program-2027.about:
The Richmond Scholars Program is the University of Richmond's most prestigious merit award. It covers full tuition, housing and food for up to eight semesters (including study abroad) and comes with a community of scholars, special programming and funding opportunities. Up to 25 incoming students are selected each year.

The university's financial aid office states that all first-year applicants are considered for the Richmond Scholars Program regardless of citizenship status, as long as they submit a complete admission application by 1 December. No separate scholarship application is needed. Richmond also meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted students who apply for need-based aid; international applicants not applying for aid complete an International Financial Certification.

Semi-finalists and finalists are invited to further selection steps in early spring.
highlights: Full tuition, housing and food for eight semesters
Open regardless of citizenship
No separate application: complete your file by 1 December
richmond-scholars-program-2027.eligibility: All first-year applicants, US and international, with a complete admission application by 1 Dec 2026. Transfer students are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Submit the Common App to the University of Richmond by 1 Dec 2026
Make sure transcripts, recommendations and (if needed) English test scores arrive by the deadline
Apply for need-based aid or submit the International Financial Certification
Take part in finalist activities if invited
richmond-scholars-program-2027.costs: Full tuition, housing and food, renewable for up to eight consecutive semesters.

soka-opportunity-plan-international-2027.about:
Soka University of America is a small liberal arts college in Southern California with a highly international student body and a required study-abroad semester. Through the updated Soka Opportunity Plan, from the 2027–2028 academic year every eligible family with total income of US$200,000 or less gets 100% tuition covered; incomes of US$200,001–250,000 get 50% and US$250,001–300,000 get 25%.

Every admitted undergraduate automatically receives a merit scholarship regardless of income, which counts towards the guarantee. International students are eligible for need-based aid through the Soka International Student Financial Aid Application, and students with the highest need can receive grants beyond tuition.

Apply for admission by 1 November 2026 (Early Action) or 15 January 2027 (Regular). The international aid application is expected to open on 1 November; apply by 15 February 2027 for an aid offer in March (final deadline 2 March).
highlights: 100% tuition for family income ≤ US$200,000 (2027–28)
Automatic merit scholarship for every admitted student
International students eligible for need-based aid
soka-opportunity-plan-international-2027.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality. Need-based aid requires the Soka International Student Financial Aid Application with supporting documents. Soka prefers TOEFL iBT 100 / Duolingo 130 (new TOEFL scale 5) or at least TOEFL 80 / Duolingo 115 for non-native speakers.
how_to_apply: Apply via the Common App or Soka Online Application by 15 Jan 2027 (or EA by 1 Nov 2026)
Complete the Soka International Student Financial Aid Application (opens ~1 Nov)
Submit financial documents by the 15 Feb 2027 priority deadline (final 2 Mar)
Receive your aid offer in the second week of March
soka-opportunity-plan-international-2027.costs: Tuition guarantee: 100% (income ≤ US$200k), 50% (US$200–250k) or 25% (US$250–300k). Housing, meals and travel are covered only if need-based grants exceed tuition.

berea-college-international-full-aid-202.about:
Berea College in Kentucky is a liberal arts college that charges no tuition to any student and runs a mandatory Labor Program in which every student works on campus for pay. For international students, admission comes with financial aid and scholarships covering 100% of tuition, housing, food and fees, making it one of the very few fully funded US undergraduate options open to all nationalities.

Berea admits about 40 or fewer new international students each year (around 120 are enrolled, from more than 70 countries), so competition is intense and the personal essay carries particular weight. Admitted students pay a US$2,200 deposit to confirm their place (an adjustment can be requested). New international students start only in the fall term.

The deadline is strict: all components must be submitted by 30 November, with no extensions. Applicants who cannot finish by then are told to apply for the following year.
highlights: 100% of tuition, housing, food and fees for admitted internationals
Paid on-campus work for personal expenses
About 40 places a year for international students
berea-college-international-full-aid-202.eligibility: International applicants who meet their own country's university entrance requirements and do not already hold a bachelor's degree. Every applicant must submit one test score: TOEFL iBT 68, IELTS 6.0 (no band below 5), Duolingo 95, SAT 980 or ACT 19 (nursing needs TOEFL 83).
how_to_apply: Create an account on Berea's online application portal
Submit the application, essay, transcripts, recommendations and test score by 30 Nov 2026
Wait for the decision by 31 March 2027
If admitted, pay the US$2,200 enrolment deposit and complete visa forms
berea-college-international-full-aid-202.costs: Tuition, housing, food and fees fully covered; students pay a US$2,200 deposit and their own personal expenses (helped by campus work earnings).

davis-uwc-scholars-2027.about:
Founded by philanthropist Shelby M.C. Davis, the Davis United World College Scholars Program has supported more than 4,600 scholars. It gives grants to 106 partner colleges (2026–27) across 35 US states and universities, which use them to provide need-based financial aid to graduates of the 18 United World College (UWC) schools.

It is relevant to you if you are at, or will graduate from, a UWC school (including students who entered through a UWC national committee). You apply to Davis partner colleges in the normal way, and if admitted on your own merit the college packages Davis funds with its own aid to meet your demonstrated need, which often means a full ride. Partners range from research universities to small liberal arts colleges; the current 2026–27 list is published on the Davis website.

There is no separate Davis application: deadlines are those of each partner college (mostly early November for early rounds and early January for regular decision). Davis scholars also get access to a network of thousands of alumni and summer and career opportunities.
highlights: Need-based aid at 106 US partner colleges
Often a full ride once admitted
No separate application: just be a UWC graduate
davis-uwc-scholars-2027.eligibility: Graduates of one of the 18 UWC schools (having completed the final two years of secondary school there) who gain admission on their own merit to a Davis partner college and demonstrate financial need.
how_to_apply: Check the current Davis partner list on davisuwcscholars.org
Apply to partner colleges through the Common App by their own deadlines (mostly 1–15 Jan 2027)
Submit each college's financial aid forms (CSS Profile etc.)
Admitted UWC graduates with need receive aid that includes Davis funding
davis-uwc-scholars-2027.costs: Need-based aid that meets demonstrated need (tuition, housing, food and more) at partner colleges; Davis pays grants to colleges, not to students directly.

mit-financial-aid-international-2027.about:
MIT is one of very few US universities that are both need-blind and full-need for every applicant, regardless of citizenship. Admissions never considers whether you can pay, and if you are admitted MIT meets 100% of your demonstrated financial need with scholarships, not loans in the standard package.

From the 2025–26 academic year, students whose family income is under US$200,000 a year (with typical assets) attend MIT tuition-free, and families earning under US$100,000 are not expected to contribute at all, so aid also covers housing, food and other costs. The 2026–27 full cost of attendance is about US$92,760, so for many international families this is effectively a full ride.

Apply by 1 November 2026 (Early Action, non-binding) or 4 January 2027 (Regular Action) through MIT's own application portal, then submit the CSS Profile and MIT's financial aid documents (RA: by 15 February 2027). MIT requires the SAT or ACT.
highlights: Need-blind admission for international applicants
Tuition-free under US$200k family income; US$0 under US$100k
Aid meets 100% of demonstrated need
mit-financial-aid-international-2027.eligibility: Students of any nationality applying as first-years through MIT's own application. SAT or ACT required; English proficiency test recommended for non-native speakers. Aid is based solely on demonstrated financial need (no merit scholarships).
how_to_apply: Create an account on the MIT application portal (MyMIT)
Submit the application, essays, two teacher recommendations and the school report by 4 Jan 2027 (or EA 1 Nov 2026)
Submit the CSS Profile and MIT financial aid documents by 15 Feb 2027
Receive your aid offer with your admission decision in mid-March
mit-financial-aid-international-2027.costs: Up to the full cost of attendance (≈ US$92,760 in 2026–27): tuition, housing, food, books and personal expenses, depending on family income and assets.

harvard-financial-aid-international-2027.about:
Harvard College's admission process is need-blind for every applicant, and its financial aid fact sheet states that foreign students have the same access to financial aid as US citizens, funded by Harvard's own scholarship money. Aid is entirely need-based; there are no merit scholarships.

From 2025–26, families with incomes below US$100,000 (and typical assets) are not expected to contribute anything, so aid covers tuition, housing, food, fees and more. For families below US$200,000, aid covers at least the full cost of tuition, and families above that can still qualify depending on circumstances.

Apply through the Common App by 1 November 2026 (Restrictive Early Action) or 1 January 2027 (Regular Decision) and submit the CSS Profile and Harvard's aid documents. You can compare offers and decide by 1 May.
highlights: Need-blind admission and equal aid for international students
US$0 family contribution under US$100k income
At least full tuition under US$200k income
harvard-financial-aid-international-2027.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality. Aid depends solely on demonstrated need, assessed from the CSS Profile and supporting documents.
how_to_apply: Apply via the Common App by 1 Jan 2027 (RD) or 1 Nov 2026 (REA)
Submit the CSS Profile and Harvard's financial aid documents
Receive your aid estimate with your admission decision
harvard-financial-aid-international-2027.costs: Up to the full cost of attendance (tuition, housing, food, fees and allowances) depending on family income and assets; no loans required.

yale-financial-aid-international-2027.about:
Yale College awards every dollar of undergraduate aid on the basis of need, and its aid offers meet 100% of demonstrated need regardless of a student's citizenship or immigration status, using scholarships rather than loans. Admission is need-blind, so asking for aid does not affect your chances.

For new students from 2026–27, families with typical assets and incomes below US$100,000 have all expected costs eliminated, and those below US$200,000 receive scholarships that at least cover tuition. Aid for international students includes allowances for housing, meals and travel to and from campus, and Yale accounts for differences between the US economy and your home country's.

Apply by 1 November 2026 (Single-Choice Early Action) or 2 January 2027 (Regular Decision) via the Common App, Coalition or QuestBridge. International students submit the CSS Profile and Yale's aid forms (Yale does not accept the ISFAA in their place) by 1 December (SCEA) or 15 February 2027 (RD).
highlights: Need-blind, 100% of need met without loans for all citizenships
No cost under US$100k; no tuition under US$200k
Travel allowances for international students
yale-financial-aid-international-2027.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality. Aid is solely need-based; international applicants must complete Yale's required financial aid forms (the ISFAA is not accepted instead).
how_to_apply: Apply by 2 Jan 2027 (RD) or 1 Nov 2026 (SCEA)
Complete the CSS Profile and Yale's financial aid forms
Submit aid documents by 15 Feb 2027 (RD) or 1 Dec 2026 (SCEA, internationals)
Receive your aid award with your admission decision
yale-financial-aid-international-2027.costs: Up to the full cost of attendance including housing, meals and two round trips a year, depending on need; no loans in the package.

princeton-financial-aid-international-20.about:
Princeton's admission is need-blind for all applicants, including international students, and the full need of all admitted international students is met in the same way as for students from the United States. Students who qualify receive grants that never have to be repaid; loans are not part of the standard offer.

Princeton has one of the most generous aid programmes in the world: aid covers the difference between Princeton's costs and what your family can contribute, and for many lower- and middle-income families that means tuition, housing and food are fully paid. The family contribution can vary depending on your country of residence. There are no academic or athletic merit scholarships.

Apply by 1 November 2026 (Single-Choice Early Action) or 1 January 2027 (Regular Decision) and complete the CSS Profile and Princeton's financial aid application.
highlights: Need-blind for international applicants
100% of need met with grants, no loans
Contribution adjusted for your country of residence
princeton-financial-aid-international-20.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality. All aid is need-based; complete the CSS Profile and Princeton's aid forms.
how_to_apply: Apply via the Common App or QuestBridge by 1 Jan 2027 (or SCEA 1 Nov 2026)
Complete the CSS Profile and Princeton's financial aid application
Receive your aid award with your admission decision
princeton-financial-aid-international-20.costs: Grant aid covering the difference between the full cost of attendance and the expected family contribution; often full tuition, housing and food for low- and middle-income families.

dartmouth-financial-aid-international-20.about:
Dartmouth College, the Ivy League liberal arts college in Hanover, New Hampshire, expanded its need-blind admissions policy to all international citizens beginning with the Class of 2026. Your financial need is not part of the admission decision.

Dartmouth meets the demonstrated need of all admitted undergraduates, including those from other countries. Its aid for international students includes scholarships and an allowance for travel to the US, so admitted students from low- and middle-income families can attend at little or no cost.

Apply by 1 November 2026 (binding Early Decision) or 2 January 2027 (Regular Decision) via the Common App, and submit the CSS Profile and Dartmouth's aid documents (RD: by 1 February 2027).
highlights: Need-blind for international citizens
Meets 100% of demonstrated need
Travel allowance for international students
dartmouth-financial-aid-international-20.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality. Aid is need-based and requires the CSS Profile and supporting documents.
how_to_apply: Apply via the Common App by 2 Jan 2027 (or ED by 1 Nov 2026)
Submit the CSS Profile and Dartmouth's financial aid documents (RD by 1 Feb 2027)
Receive your aid offer with the admission decision
dartmouth-financial-aid-international-20.costs: Scholarships meeting full demonstrated need, up to the full cost of attendance, plus a travel allowance.

amherst-financial-aid-international-2027.about:
Amherst College in Massachusetts is consistently ranked among the best liberal arts colleges in the US. It follows a need-blind policy for international applicants and awards financial aid to international students on the same need basis as domestic students, which lets it admit the most promising students from around the world without regard to ability to pay.

Aid is entirely need-based and meets full demonstrated need, so admitted students from low-income families can attend with tuition, housing and food covered. Classes are small and taught by faculty, and Amherst students can also take courses at the other Five College Consortium schools (including UMass Amherst, Smith and Mount Holyoke).

Apply through the Common App or QuestBridge by 5 January 2027 (Regular Decision) or the November Early Decision deadline, and submit the CSS Profile with Amherst's aid documents.
highlights: Need-blind admission for international students
Aid on the same need basis as US students
Small classes plus the Five College Consortium
amherst-financial-aid-international-2027.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality; aid based on demonstrated need. Non-native English speakers submit TOEFL, IELTS Academic or another accepted English test.
how_to_apply: Apply via the Common App or QuestBridge by 5 Jan 2027
Submit the CSS Profile and Amherst's financial aid documents
Receive your need-based aid offer with your admission decision
amherst-financial-aid-international-2027.costs: Need-based aid up to the full cost of attendance (tuition, housing, food and allowances).

bowdoin-financial-aid-international-2027.about:
Bowdoin College on the coast of Maine is a highly selective liberal arts college and one of the few US colleges that is need-blind for international students. Your family's ability to pay is never a factor in admission, and if admitted Bowdoin meets your full calculated need using scholarships, with US$0 of loans in its aid packages.

A practical advantage for internationals: Bowdoin asks international applicants (except Canadians) to submit financial aid materials only if they are admitted, so you can focus on the application first. Regular Decision and Early Decision II applications are due 5 January 2027 (ED I: 15 November 2026), and regular decisions are released in mid-March.
highlights: Need-blind for international applicants
Full need met with US$0 loans
Aid forms only after you are admitted
bowdoin-financial-aid-international-2027.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality. Aid is based on calculated need; international applicants file aid forms after admission.
how_to_apply: Apply via the Common App or QuestBridge by 5 Jan 2027 (ED I: 15 Nov 2026)
If admitted, submit Bowdoin's international financial aid materials
Receive your scholarship package
bowdoin-financial-aid-international-2027.costs: Scholarships meeting full calculated need, up to the full cost of attendance, with no loans.

ucl-global-undergraduate-scholarship-202.about:
The UCL Global Undergraduate Scholarship helps international students from low-income backgrounds take a full-time bachelor's degree at University College London, one of the world's top-10 universities. In the latest round UCL offered up to 33 awards: 10 covering full tuition fees plus a maintenance allowance and a fixed allowance for extras such as the visa and Immigration Health Surcharge, 20 covering full tuition only, and 3 full-tuition awards reserved for students from India.

Selection is purely on financial need. UCL treats a household income of about £42,875 or less as 'low income', but it still considers applicants above that figure. Shortlisted candidates send financial evidence in mid-May and results come out in early June, before the UCAS reply deadline. The award runs for the standard length of the degree.

It is one of very few UK scholarships that can cover the whole cost of a degree for an international student, so if your family cannot pay London fees it is worth applying the moment UCL confirms your fee status.
highlights: Up to 10 full-cost awards (tuition + living + visa/IHS) and ~23 full-tuition awards
Need-based: no separate merit test, open to every country outside the UK
No offer needed — apply once UCL confirms your overseas fee status
ucl-global-undergraduate-scholarship-202.eligibility: Applicants from any country outside the UK who pay the overseas fee rate, come from a low-income household, and have applied (via UCAS) for a full-time UCL undergraduate degree starting in 2027. An offer is not required, but UCL Admissions must have confirmed your fee status before the form appears in Portico.
how_to_apply: Apply to UCL through UCAS (equal-consideration deadline 13 January 2027 for most courses)
Wait for UCL to confirm your overseas fee status (the scholarship form then appears in Portico)
Log in to Portico → your application → Funding → 'Check and apply' and complete the UCL Global Undergraduate Scholarship form
Submit before the late-April 2027 deadline; send financial evidence if shortlisted in May
Results are emailed in early June 2027
ucl-global-undergraduate-scholarship-202.costs: Full-cost awards: full overseas tuition (about £30,000–£45,000 a year depending on course) plus a maintenance allowance and fixed allowance for visa/IHS. Tuition-only awards: full overseas tuition, living costs not covered.

reach-oxford-scholarship-2027.about:
Reach Oxford Scholarships (formerly Oxford Student Scholarships) are for students from countries that receive official development assistance who, for political or financial reasons or because suitable education does not exist, cannot study for a degree at home. The list of eligible nationalities is long and includes, among others, Georgia, Türkiye, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, India, Pakistan, Nigeria, Kenya, Ukraine and Brazil.

The award pays course fees, a grant for living costs and one return air fare each year for the full 3–4 years of the degree. It can be held in any subject except Medicine, at any college. Selection looks at the highest academic ability, financial need, social commitment and the intention to return home after graduating. Only around 2–3 scholarships are given each year, so it is extremely competitive.

For 2027 entry the scholarship application window opens in January 2027 and closes on 26 January 2027; you can only apply if you already applied to Oxford by 15 October 2026 and received an offer. Students who missed that UCAS deadline should plan for 2028 entry.
highlights: Covers course fees, living-cost grant and an annual return flight
Open to nationals of ~140 OECD-DAC countries, all subjects except Medicine
Only 2–3 awards a year — the most selective UK undergraduate scholarship
reach-oxford-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Nationals of an OECD-DAC (official development assistance) country who hold an offer for an Oxford undergraduate course starting in October 2027 (any subject except Medicine), are of the highest academic ability, have financial need and intend to return home after study. Priority to those who have not studied at undergraduate level before.
how_to_apply: Apply to Oxford via UCAS by 15 October 2026 (already closed for 2027 entry) and receive an offer
From January 2027, follow the application instructions published on the Reach Oxford page
Submit the scholarship application by 26 January 2027
Selection takes place in April 2027; outcomes by the end of May 2027
reach-oxford-scholarship-2027.costs: Full course fees, a grant for living costs and one return air fare per year, for 3 or 4 years. Renewal depends on satisfactory academic progress.

cambridge-trust-global-impact-scholarshi.about:
The Cambridge Trust is the University of Cambridge's main funder of international students. Its Global Impact Scholarship is aimed at undergraduate applicants with overseas fee status and a high level of financial need who have overcome significant challenges to win a place at Cambridge. It can be held at any College and in any subject.

The value is a full package: the international University tuition fee, the College fee, annual maintenance sufficient for a single student, the student visa and the Immigration Health Surcharge. There is no separate scholarship application before admission: once a College makes you an offer, it sends you the Cambridge Trust application and you are considered for every Trust award you qualify for. Most awards are made in February and March.

For 2027 entry, the UCAS deadline for Cambridge was 15 October 2026, so this record is relevant for students who applied in that round (and for anyone planning 2028 entry). Cambridge's general undergraduate funding for internationals is limited, which makes this one of the few routes to a fully funded Cambridge degree.
highlights: Covers international tuition, College fee, maintenance, visa and IHS
Any subject, any College
Applied for after a Cambridge offer — the College sends you the Trust form
cambridge-trust-global-impact-scholarshi.eligibility: Undergraduate applicants with overseas fee status, a high level of financial need and evidence of having overcome significant challenges, who hold an offer from a Cambridge College.
how_to_apply: Apply to Cambridge via UCAS by 15 October (closed for 2027 entry; next round October 2027 for 2028 entry)
Receive an offer from a Cambridge College
Complete the Cambridge Trust application form your College sends you
Awards are announced mainly between mid-February and March
cambridge-trust-global-impact-scholarshi.costs: International tuition fee (roughly £27,000–£70,000 a year depending on subject), College fee, annual maintenance for a single person, student visa and Immigration Health Surcharge.

imperial-inspires-scholarship-2027.about:
Imperial Inspires is Imperial College London's large new scholarship programme for international students. For autumn 2027 entry Imperial is offering at least 300 awards of £15,000 per year, for each year of the course, across its four faculties: Engineering, Natural Sciences, Medicine and the Business School. It covers undergraduate degrees including integrated master's courses (MEng, MSci).

The scholarship is merit-based: Imperial looks for academic excellence, curiosity, initiative, leadership and a global outlook, and region of origin is not a factor. After you apply through UCAS, eligible applicants who meet the course's minimum entry requirements are invited (from October 2026) to answer an additional optional essay question, which is the scholarship application. Awards are made by mid-April 2027 and cannot be deferred.

£15,000 does not cover the full overseas fee (about £40,000+ a year), but over a four-year MEng it is worth £60,000 and can sometimes be combined with other awards.
highlights: At least 300 awards of £15,000 per year for 2027 entry
All undergraduate courses incl. MEng/MSci in Engineering, Natural Sciences, Medicine and Business
Short extra essay after your UCAS application — no separate form beforehand
imperial-inspires-scholarship-2027.eligibility: International students who will pay Imperial's overseas tuition rate and apply for a full-time undergraduate course starting in autumn 2027 that offers the scholarship, meeting the course's minimum entry requirements.
how_to_apply: Apply to Imperial through UCAS (opened 2 September 2026; deadline 13 January 2027 — apply early)
If eligible, you will be invited to complete the optional Imperial Inspires essay question
Submit the essay by the scholarship deadline (5 February 2027 per Imperial's scholarship listing)
Decisions are issued by mid-April 2027
imperial-inspires-scholarship-2027.costs: £15,000 per year towards tuition and living costs for each year of the course. Overseas tuition at Imperial is about £40,000–£50,000+ a year, so the rest must be self-funded.

lse-undergraduate-support-scheme-2027.about:
The LSE Undergraduate Support Scheme (USS) is the London School of Economics' main financial aid for international undergraduates. It is for students with overseas fee status, holding an offer for any LSE bachelor's programme, who do not have the funds to cover all their costs of study.

Awards are tailored to each student's circumstances and are usually between £15,000 and £25,000 per year, renewed for each year of the programme subject to satisfactory progress. LSE receives far more applications than it can fund, so not every applicant succeeds. LSE also runs donor-funded scholarships (for example the Uggla Family Scholars Programme) that can be combined with USS.

LSE is one of the world's leading social-science universities (economics, international relations, politics, law, finance). The scheme makes it realistic for strong students from middle-income families to attend.
highlights: Typically £15,000–£25,000 a year, renewed for the full degree
Open to overseas-fee students on any LSE undergraduate programme
Based on financial need, assessed after you receive an offer
lse-undergraduate-support-scheme-2027.eligibility: Overseas fee status students holding an offer for any LSE undergraduate programme starting in 2027 who cannot meet the full costs of study.
how_to_apply: Apply to LSE through UCAS by 13 January 2027
Receive an offer
Complete LSE's undergraduate financial support application (linked from your offer pack and the Fees and funding pages)
Submit before the overseas financial-support deadline (around late April 2027) with evidence of household income
lse-undergraduate-support-scheme-2027.costs: Usually £15,000–£25,000 per year towards costs. LSE overseas tuition is about £28,000–£30,000 a year plus London living costs.

edinburgh-global-undergraduate-mathemati.about:
The Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarships are awarded by the University of Edinburgh to international applicants with outstanding academic results who are accepted for full-time undergraduate study in the School of Mathematics (degrees in mathematics, statistics and their joint programmes).

Each scholarship is worth £5,000, paid in instalments towards living costs, and continues for the length of the programme as long as you make satisfactory progress. Several awards are made each year. You must have applied via UCAS, but you can complete the scholarship application before receiving an offer.

Edinburgh's School of Mathematics is one of the strongest in the UK, and Scottish four-year degrees give a broad first year. The award is modest compared with overseas fees, but it is renewable and relatively accessible for strong maths students.
highlights: £5,000 per year for the whole degree
For international/EU-fee students in the School of Mathematics
Deadline 31 March 2027; results 23 April 2027
edinburgh-global-undergraduate-mathemati.eligibility: Applicants with international/EU fee status accepted for full-time undergraduate study in Edinburgh's School of Mathematics (not current students, not maths taken in another School), with outstanding academic performance.
how_to_apply: Apply for an undergraduate mathematics degree at Edinburgh through UCAS
Complete the scholarship application linked from the scholarship page (an offer is not required)
Submit by 23:59 UK time on 31 March 2027
Decisions are sent on 23 April 2027
edinburgh-global-undergraduate-mathemati.costs: £5,000 a year towards living costs. Overseas tuition (about £30,000+ a year) is not covered.

st-andrews-international-undergraduate-s.about:
The University of St Andrews, Scotland's oldest university and consistently near the top of UK league tables, offers International Undergraduate Scholarships to students with overseas fee status beginning an undergraduate degree in 2027. The award is a tuition-fee reduction applied every year of the degree.

It is assessed on financial need. Applicants are encouraged to describe circumstances such as a case for financial need, previous needs-based funding, a disadvantaged neighbourhood, a disability or belonging to a minority group. You enter your gross annual household income in GBP. The course and funding applications are independent, so applying does not affect your admission decision. A separate Accommodation Award (£1,900 a year) shares the same deadline.

The exact value will be confirmed by December 2026. It is available in almost every School (from Computer Science and International Relations to Medicine), but not for the joint BA International Honours with William & Mary, which has its own scholarship.
highlights: Annual tuition-fee reduction for the whole degree
Need-based; no offer required to apply
Closes 27 January 2027 — results mid-March 2027
st-andrews-international-undergraduate-s.eligibility: Students with overseas fee status entering the first year (or direct entry to second year) of a St Andrews undergraduate degree in 2027, with financial need. Transfer students and the William & Mary joint BA are excluded.
how_to_apply: Apply to St Andrews via UCAS or the Common Application (equal-consideration deadline 13 January 2027)
Two working days later, log in to the My Application portal
Complete the International Undergraduate Scholarships form with household income details
Submit by 27 January 2027; results the week of 17 March 2027
st-andrews-international-undergraduate-s.costs: Tuition-fee reduction each year (value confirmed by December 2026). Overseas tuition is roughly £33,000–£38,000 a year; living costs are not covered (a separate £1,900/yr Accommodation Award exists).

durham-inspiring-excellence-undergraduat.about:
Durham University's Inspiring Excellence Undergraduate Scholarship is a competitive, merit-based partial award for international applicants. It comes in two sizes: £5,000 per year (up to £15,000 over a three-year degree) or £10,000 per year (up to £30,000), applied as a discount on tuition for programmes starting in September 2027.

Selection considers your scholarship answers, academic achievement and potential to make a positive impact, while also balancing nationalities and programmes. You do not need an offer to apply, only a UCAS ID. If you are not selected in round 1, you are automatically reconsidered in round 2. Successful students must make Durham their Firm Choice by the UCAS reply deadline.

Durham is a collegiate top-10 UK university known for law, economics, natural sciences, history and engineering. Note the restrictions: the award cannot be combined with any other scholarship or sponsorship, and it excludes Clearing, the International Study Centre route and two theology degrees.
highlights: £5,000 or £10,000 off tuition every year (up to £30,000)
Three rounds: 7 Dec 2026, 15 Mar 2027, 1 May 2027
No offer needed to apply — just a UCAS ID
durham-inspiring-excellence-undergraduat.eligibility: Self-funded applicants with overseas fee status, applying to a full-time in-person Durham undergraduate programme starting September 2027, who meet the entry requirements, hold no other scholarship or sponsorship, and make Durham their Firm (not Insurance) choice. Not via Clearing or the International Study Centre; BA Theology, Ministry and Mission and BA Theology and Religion excluded.
how_to_apply: Apply to Durham via UCAS (equal-consideration deadline 13 January 2027, 18:00 UK)
Complete the Inspiring Excellence Undergraduate Scholarship online form with your UCAS ID
Submit by 7 December 2026 (round 1), 15 March 2027 (round 2) or 1 May 2027 (final)
If successful, make Durham your Firm Choice by the UCAS reply date
durham-inspiring-excellence-undergraduat.costs: Tuition discount of £5,000 or £10,000 per year for up to three years. Overseas tuition is around £30,000–£38,000 a year; living costs are not covered.

bristol-think-big-undergraduate-scholars.about:
Think Big is the University of Bristol's main scholarship scheme for international students. For undergraduates starting in September 2027 the awards are worth £6,500 or £13,000 per year for up to four years of study, applied as a reduction in tuition fees rather than paid as cash.

You must be classed as an overseas student for fees and have applied, or be about to apply, for an eligible in-person undergraduate course. You do not need an offer before applying. The single online form also puts you forward for other awards you qualify for, such as GREAT Scholarships and some donor bursaries. Outcomes are sent by the end of May 2027.

Bristol is a Russell Group university ranked in the global top 60, strong in engineering, computer science, economics, law and the life sciences.
highlights: £6,500 or £13,000 per year for up to four years
One form also considers you for GREAT and other Bristol awards
Closes 19 March 2027 — no offer required
bristol-think-big-undergraduate-scholars.eligibility: Students with overseas fee status who have applied, or will apply, for a full-time in-person Bristol undergraduate course (up to four years) starting September 2027. Online, distance and part-time courses are excluded.
how_to_apply: Apply for your Bristol course through UCAS
Complete the international scholarships online form linked from the Think Big page
Submit before 1pm UK time on 19 March 2027
Outcomes by end of May 2027; accept the award by the stated deadline
bristol-think-big-undergraduate-scholars.costs: Tuition reduction of £6,500 or £13,000 per year. Overseas tuition is roughly £27,000–£35,000 a year; living costs are not covered.

glasgow-world-changers-global-excellence.about:
The University of Glasgow's World Changers Global Excellence Scholarship rewards international and EU (non-UK) undergraduates with excellent grades. For 2027 entry it is a tuition-fee discount of £10,000 a year in the Colleges of Medical, Veterinary & Life Sciences and Science & Engineering, and £7,000 a year in Arts and Social Sciences, renewed annually with satisfactory progress.

There is no application form: everyone who receives an offer is automatically assessed against published grade thresholds (achieved or predicted), for example AAB / IB 36 for most sciences and humanities, AAA / IB 38 for psychology and the Adam Smith Business School, and A*AA / IB 39 for law, computing science and James Watt MEng. Medicine, Dentistry and Veterinary Medicine are excluded. Candidates under consideration hear within two weeks of their offer.

Glasgow is a Russell Group university in the world top 80, and Scottish four-year degrees give flexibility in the first two years.
highlights: £7,000–£10,000 off tuition every year
Automatic — no separate application
Clear grade thresholds (e.g. IB 36–40 / A-levels AAB–A*A*A)
glasgow-world-changers-global-excellence.eligibility: International or EU (non-UK) fee-status students with an offer for an eligible Glasgow undergraduate programme starting in 2027 who meet the published A-level/IB (or equivalent) thresholds. Medicine, Dentistry and Veterinary Medicine excluded.
how_to_apply: Apply to Glasgow through UCAS (equal-consideration deadline 13 January 2027)
Meet or be predicted the scholarship grade threshold for your programme
Receive an offer — you are assessed automatically
Glasgow contacts you within two weeks if you are being considered
glasgow-world-changers-global-excellence.costs: Tuition discount of £10,000 or £7,000 per year. Overseas tuition is about £25,000–£32,000 a year (higher for clinical subjects); living costs are not covered.

manchester-global-futures-scholarship-20.about:
